sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $31.7 billion [F198][F9].
Operating income grew faster, at a 5.8% CAGR to $8.6 billion, lifting operating margin from 22.9% to 27.2% [F199][F19][F20][F28].
FY2022 was the step change: revenue rose 17.1% to $28.7 billion on higher retail sales volumes and favorable weather [D239][F6][P33].
FY2020 was the trough, with net income down 63.3% to $1.4 billion on coal ash impairment charges and COVID-19 volume declines [D157][F33][P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue and 3.6pp of its 5.6% growth [D541][D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest customer class at 43.3% of revenue, contributing 2.8pp of FY2025 growth [D774][D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure added 2.0pp in FY2025, with Piedmont Natural Gas revenue up 32.1% [D566][D682].
Operating costs grew 0.3pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 5.3%, and incremental operating margin was 41.4% [D379][D372][D378].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% a year against 9.7% net income growth as the diluted share count rose from 691 million to 777 million [F202][F200][X106][X115].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% was the window high, above the 22.9% median and the 19.7% low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
D&A rose to 24.3% of revenue in FY2025 from 21.4%, a 2.9pp drag, while operating margin still gained 0.8pp [D341][D303][D370].
FY2024's 1.7pp margin gain came with net income up 59.2% to $4.5 billion, helped by rate increases and riders and by prior-year Commercial Renewables impairments [D330][D320][F37][P18].
In FY2025 net margin of 15.7% sat 11.5pp below the 27.2% operating margin, as interest expense of $3.6 billion and an 11.2% tax rate absorbed the gap [F47][F28][D967][X63][D345].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, below the 2.59x window median [F77][F38][D346][D958].
Free cash flow was negative $1.7 billion, a -5.3% margin, against a -5.8% window median [F97][D343][D939].
Capex of $14.0 billion was 44.2% of revenue and 1.82x D&A [F87][D342][D348].
FY2022 operating cash flow fell 28.5% to $5.9 billion as rising fuel costs created undercollections financed with borrowings [D244][F74][P36].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025, with total debt of $89.8 billion against $245 million of cash [D352][D351][D350].
Net cash was -282.3% of revenue, below the -235.4% peer median, at the 33rd percentile of three peers [D353][D969][D968].
The current ratio fell to 0.55x, below the 0.66x window median, as current liabilities rose 8.7% to $21.0 billion [F177][D945][D369][F157].
Return on average equity of 9.7% was below the 12.6% peer median, at the 0th percentile of four peers [D357][D956][D955].
Debt issued of $11.9 billion exceeded $5.7 billion repaid in FY2025, and the diluted share count rose 0.6% [X133][X143][D374].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year and fell to 0.55x in FY2025 [F177][F168].
For a regulated utility this reflects routine short-term debt rollover rather than distress, but it leaves little liquidity cushion [F177].
Net debt rose for nine straight years, from $50.0 billion in FY2016 to $89.6 billion in FY2025 [D14][D352].
Debt-funded capex is the growth engine here, so the leverage trend is structural, with total debt growth of 6.6% in FY2025 [D376].
Free cash flow was below 80% of net income in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at -0.96x, 0.01x and -0.34x [D269][D309][D347].
Persistent negative free cash flow means dividends and capex depend on continued debt access, and cash covers only 0.1 years of burn [D356].
Whether FY2026 operating margin holds above the 22.9% window median or slips from the 27.2% FY2025 high, in the FY2026 10-K [D933][F28].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -282.3% toward the -235.4% peer median, in the FY2026 10-K [D353][D969].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers from -5.3% toward the 0.2% window high, in the FY2026 10-K [D343][D938].
